body.subject: Codex judge verdict: item48-balances-chain-order-r5 = C
body.text: artifact=item48-balances-chain-order-r5 kind=code purpose=tri7 item 48 round 5 — one file changed since round 4 (A): the live-DNS3 taught the acceptance check that a build finishing short of the advancing tip (bodies lag) is PENDING (the node schedules an incremental retry and converges), not a rejection; verdict now taken from the last finished build; 19-case selftest incl. both live shapes; the canary's own evidence shows the fix's trigger (index-order build done h2219460 vs chased h2219462, retry in 60s, next start from the new snapshot) and the clean rollback. Decisions: commit this checker fix and re-deploy per brief section 7 worktree=/tmp/codex-judge-ANoFUL codex_grade=C judge=codex
reasons: The checker’s 19-case self-test passes, and the core last-build/pending-retry behavior handles the documented DNS3 journal shape.

The packaged checker SHA-256 is 5af7a9d06e73a9b112a61493f0653b7898111b1f6f283526aa4820171c90d90e, but 7_source_sha256.txt records the previous checker hash 6049e94892397989108cd40d92479509ebab83c6b441caf857c569936a751de2. Thus the final bytes proposed for commit are not tied to the supplied source manifest.

2_balances_chain_ordered.py claims the next DNS3 build converged, but 4_ev_deploy_dns3.txt shows rollback before that retry completed; it supports only that the retry was scheduled and began from the new snapshot.
RETRY captures coverage and chased heights but judge() ignores them, so any later matching retry line can mark a short finished build pending even if the line does not correspond to that build.
blocking_issues: Regenerate 7_source_sha256.txt for the actual round-5 checker bytes before promotion.
Remove or substantiate the claim that live DNS3’s next build converged; the packaged live transcript does not demonstrate convergence.
Associate a retry line with the finished build by verifying its captured coverage/chased heights, and add mismatched-retry and unrelated-retry self-tests.
